$comment: Fixture #3: a procedure-calling island, LIVE against demo-app's /island/search. The first fixture that crosses the network boundary and the first that measures an INTERVAL. See `$landed` for the three ways the island that shipped differs from the shape this was scaffolded against, and why none of them moved an expectation.
name: search
$events: Two, and `input` is the interesting one: the counter and the nested fixture both only delegate `click`, so this is the first fixture that proves the bootstrap's event list is derived from the island's handlers rather than hardcoded. run.mjs compares the served bootstrap against `buildHydrationScript(events)` for exactly this list, so a server that delegated only `click` fails before any typing happens.
sourceShape: The island as it SHIPPED, `demo-app/island/search.rs`, kept here so this file
says what it is measuring. Read `$landed.divergences` for how it differs from
the shape originally scaffolded and why nothing below moved.
signal query = no_query();      // String on the server, &'static str in the browser
signal replies = 0.0;           // an ANSWER COUNTER, not the answers
<input class="search-input" type="text" placeholder="..."
@input=$(|e| { let e: Ev = e; query.set(e.target_value()) })>
<ul class="search-results">
for item in hits(query.get(), replies) {
• (item)
`hits` is declared once per target: the server's returns an empty Vec (it has
asked nothing), the browser's reads `replies` for the SUBSCRIPTION, calls the
host's `search_ask`, and iterates the rows of the last reply. So reading the
answer is what asks for the next one, and `replies` is what brings it back.
THE DEBOUNCE lives in `demo-app/src/island-rt.mjs`, which is the page's own
module rather than compiled Rust. This fixture never required a particular
place for it: what it measures is a settling window of `expected.debounceMs`,
one call per settled query, and no call while the user is still typing.
NO SEEDS. The island takes no arguments, so `data-ts` is `[]` and the compiled
entry point's arity is 0. That is itself worth having: the counter fixture pins
the one-argument case and nothing else pins zero, which is the case where a
loader passing `undefined` rather than nothing would still appear to work.

wire.$what: The procedure wire the island's client half speaks. Every value here is CHECKED against contract/fixtures/procedure-wire.json by lib/wire.mjs, on every run including while this fixture is pending. So this block cannot drift from the spec, and the stub interact.mjs builds from it cannot be a convenient approximation.
wire.$wireWhy: The serde wire, not the surrogate one: a procedure returning Vec<String> to a Rust-compiled client is exactly what that wire exists for. procedure-wire.json `wires.serde.$exclusive` records that a serde procedure cannot be named from expr! at all, so this island cannot use the surrogate path even by accident.
wire.$zeroArguments: Recorded even though this island always sends one argument, because it is the asymmetry most likely to be got wrong: the SURROGATE wire spells zero arguments `null` and each wire rejects the other's spelling. interact.mjs asserts the island never sends `null`.
wire.$errorBody: The middle of this message is serde_json's own wording and MUST NOT be asserted -- a patch release would break the test. Prefix and suffix only. The suffix is DERIVED from the spec's $pathRule at `errorArgumentIndex`, not copied: the rule is that segments join with `.` and a sequence index is written `[n]`, and the argument array is a sequence.
wire.$idIsNotKnowable: A procedure's id is a v4 uuid minted at MACRO-EXPANSION time, so it is not stable across rebuilds and cannot be written down here. The fixture asserts the route SHAPE -- the prefix plus exactly one non-empty segment -- which is everything about the URL that is knowable from the client side.
wire.$vectors: The vectors this fixture honours, by id. lib/wire.mjs asserts each one exists and that the values above are the ones it carries. Naming them rather than copying them is the whole mechanism: when a vector was corrected in wave 2, a fixture that had copied the value would have kept sending the stale one into a stub that accepted it happily.
wire.$ifTheIslandDivergesFromThis: The framework agent's host-call design may hit a demo-app route rather than the procedure route (their finding: a procedure id is minted per expansion, so one #[procedure] in a file shared by the server and client crates gets TWO different uuids and cannot address itself). If so: move `routePrefix` to what the island calls and record the divergence, but KEEP the body encoding, the media type and the error vectors -- those are what this fixture is for, and they are the part their design preserves.

callTarget.$why: NOT the procedure route, and this is a finding rather than a shortcut. A procedure's id is a v4 uuid minted at MACRO-EXPANSION time, and an island's file is expanded TWICE -- once by the server crate, once by the client crate -- so the two expansions mint DIFFERENT ids and a procedure declared in a file shared by both halves cannot address itself from the client. demo-app's answer (framework agent, wave-3 item 3) is a written-down `#[route(POST "/demo/search")]` decoding through `topcoat::runtime::serde_args`, so the SAME wire is served at a URL that does not depend on an expansion. The `#[procedure(serde)] fn search` exists beside it as the surface an app uses.
callTarget.$whatThisFixtureStillProves: Everything it was for. The route changed; the wire did not. Media type, argument array encoding, zero-argument asymmetry, response encoding and the error shape are all unchanged, and those are what the vectors below pin. This is exactly the move `$ifTheIslandDivergesFromThis` prescribed before the divergence happened.

wire.$routePrefixNote: Kept and still cross-checked against procedure-wire.json, because the procedure route DOES exist for `#[procedure(serde)] fn search` -- it is just not what a compiled island can call. `fetchStub` reports both `isProcedureRoute` and `onTarget` so a fixture can tell which it got.
wire.$errorArgumentIndex: THIS procedure takes ONE argument, so a bad argument is index 0 and the server answers ``(at `[0]`)``. MEASURED live by the framework agent with curl against `POST /demo/search`. The vector below pins a TWO-argument signature, hence its `[1]`: same rule, different index. lib/wire.mjs therefore validates the spec's $pathRule against the vector's own recorded suffix FIRST and only then applies it here, so copying a literal that the real server never sends is not possible.
wire.$errorVectorArgumentIndex: The index the VECTOR's own bad argument sits at. Present so the rule check is a closed loop with no free parameter: if rule(1) stops rendering the vector's recorded suffix, either the rule or the vector moved, and the fixture must not be edited to paper over it.

expected.$keys: One key: the island's own template root. No components, so nothing nests. The result list's <li>s are created by the CLIENT after the procedure answers, so they carry no server key at all -- which is why `hydrateMutations` below is still 0 and the list starts empty.
expected.$templates: Two: the island's own, and the <li> the `for` body declares. A loop body is its own template root even with no components in the source, which is why this fixture also exercises run.mjs's multi-template path from a different direction than `nested` does.
expected.$islandTemplate: Which declared template is the island's own root. PREDICTED as 0 and not verified: if the emitter declares the loop body first, run.mjs's template-order diagnostic will say so by index and this becomes 1. That is a scaffold assumption, labelled as one.
expected.$debounceMs: The settling window. The fixture asserts NO call before it and exactly one after, sampling at `debounceMs * 0.4` for the negative half so the assertion is not a race against its own timer. If the island's window is not 150, change this ONE number.
expected.$queries: Two, because a fixture that only ran one query could not tell rendering from re-rendering: the second one asserts the list is REPLACED and not appended to.
expected.$results: MEASURED, not invented: these are the bodies `POST /demo/search` actually answered for `["ru"]` and `["st"]`, recorded by the framework agent's live curl run against demo-app's CATALOGUE of 15 words. The two lists OVERLAP on "rust" and "trust", which is what makes the replace-vs-append assertion sharp: a list rendered by appending would read as seven items, and a disjoint pair would make an append look like a replace to anyone reading only the last item.
expected.$clickMutations: Not applicable: this island's update is driven by a procedure reply, not a click, and the mutation counts it produces are asserted in interact.mjs against the list's own content rather than declared as a single number here. Recorded as null so it is clear the omission is deliberate.

$landed.$what: Recorded because a scaffold that is quietly edited to match what shipped proves nothing. These are the differences between what this fixture predicted and what landed, each with whether it moved an expectation.
divergences: SOURCE SHAPE, changed by them, no expectation moved. The scaffold predicted `signal results = Vec<String>` filled by the reply and `for item in $(results.get())`. What shipped is two signals -- `query` and `replies: f64`, an ANSWER COUNTER -- and `for item in hits(query.get(), replies)`, where `hits` is declared once per target. Forced, not chosen: the island crate is `#![no_std]` with no heap, so a decoded `Vec<String>` is not a value it can hold, and a `$( )` cannot spell a host call. The reply stays as parsed JSON on the page side and is read a row at a time. Every expectation below survives it, because all of them are about the DOM and the wire rather than about how the island holds its state.

THE CALL IS MADE BY THE PAGE, not by compiled Rust. `search_ask(url, query, ms, replies)` is an `extern "C"` the island declares and `demo-app/src/island-rt.mjs` implements, so the fetch, the 150ms timer and the JSON parse all live in that module. This fixture measures the wire that leaves the page, which is the same wire either way -- and that is the point: the fixture is written against the bytes on the socket, so it did not care which side of the boundary produced them.

THE DEBOUNCE IS COALESCED BY A GUARD AS WELL AS A TIMER. `island-rt.mjs` keeps `asked` and returns early when the query has not changed, because asking is a side effect of READING the answer and without the guard the reply's own signal write would ask again forever. Consequence this fixture has to respect: a repeated keystroke of the same value is a no-op, so the three keystrokes below are two distinct values plus a repeat, and the coalescing that is actually proved is the timer reset between the first two.

`/demo/islands.js` IS GONE, which the pending block's fourth condition named. The island's client half is `/demo/chunks/search.js`, resolved through the page's own import map by `topcoat-island/search`. run.mjs now follows the map rather than a path it builds itself.
$landed.conditionsMet: All six of the former `flipsWhen` conditions hold, the fourth in the amended form above. The wire, the debounce window, the media type and the argument encoding are exactly what `wire` declares -- confirmed independently by the framework agent's own smoke run before this was flipped.
